updates.name: Stuart E. Jones
updates.bio: Aquatic ecologist and Executive Director of Grand Valley State University's Annis Water Resources Institute, where his lab pairs simple mathematical models with field observations to understand lakes and their watersheds. Current projects address recreational fisheries as coupled social-ecological systems, controls on lake productivity and water quality, and lake carbon cycling and climate feedbacks.
updates.research_interests: recreational fisheries dynamics (social-ecological systems); regulation of lake primary productivity and water quality; carbon cycling and lake-mediated climate feedbacks

updates.bio: Emeritus Professor in Arizona State University's School of Life Sciences and an affiliate Global Futures Scholar. updates.bio: Research ecologist with the USDA Forest Service Pacific Southwest Research Station, trained in botany at the University of Hawaii (PhD 1999). Her recent publications focus on Hawaiian and Micronesian forests: restoring invaded lowland wet and dry forests, seedling regeneration and phenology of endemic trees, functional traits and drought resilience, and fire regimes and land-cover change in Palau.

updates.name: Susan E. Wijffels
updates.bio: Senior Scientist in the Physical Oceanography department at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution since 2017, following more than two decades as a research scientist at Australia's CSIRO; PhD from the MIT/WHOI Joint Program. She studies the ocean's role in climate, large-scale circulation, Indonesian Throughflow variability and decadal ocean change, and co-chairs the International Argo Steering Team.
updates.research_interests: ocean's role in climate; large-scale ocean circulation; Indonesian Throughflow variability; decadal ocean variability and global ocean change; Argo array design and Global Ocean Observing System

updates.bio: Biological oceanographer (University of Washington PhD, 1990) at Western Washington University's Shannon Point Marine Center, now listed there as a retired senior research scientist. Her lab studies how plankton food webs work, the part plankton play in marine biogeochemistry, and the biology of marine protozoa, and has supported Northern Gulf of Alaska LTER work.
updates.research_interests: planktonic food web interactions; role of planktonic organisms in marine biogeochemistry; physiology, ecology and functional morphology of marine protozoa

updates.name: T'ai H. Roulston
updates.bio: Curator of the State Arboretum of Virginia and Research Associate Professor at the University of Virginia's Blandy Experimental Farm. His lab examines how plants and insects interact ecologically and evolutionarily, with a conservation emphasis: wild pollinators on farms, bumble bee and mason bee population dynamics, bees and their conopid fly parasitoids, and butternut tree conservation.
updates.research_interests: butternut (Juglans cinerea) conservation; bumble bee population dynamics and parasitism (RFID tracking); ecosystem services of wild pollinators in agriculture; evolutionary ecology of bees and conopid parasitoid flies; mason bee (Osmia) population dynamics

updates.name: Tamara E. C. Kraus
updates.bio: Research soil scientist and acting biogeochemistry program chief at the USGS California Water Science Center in Sacramento, where she has worked since 2004 after a UC Davis doctorate in soils and biogeochemistry. Her research follows carbon and nutrients between land and water: drinking-water organic-carbon sources, subsidence-reversal wetlands, coagulation-based mercury removal and nutrient-phytoplankton links.
updates.research_interests: carbon and nutrient cycling; terrestrial-aquatic linkages; dissolved organic carbon sources and drinking-water quality; constructed wetlands for subsidence reversal; in situ coagulation to remove mercury; nutrient-phytoplankton links
